objective: At the owner's request, under G18: challenge the assumption that a pattern must have a state of the whole and the narrower one beneath it, that every two distinctions have a joint value even where no knot holds both. Read patterns part by part (each view consistent, the views not required to fit one whole), test which such patterns growth reaches, run the advisor's fixture and cheapest operator check, say whether the closing sign is exactly the cost of reordering, and ask what native rule would hold such patterns below the no-signalling maximum.
status: Complete 2026-11-26 (referee pending): read part by part, patterns with no whole state give certainty where a list of values cannot, but part counting alone reaches CHSH 4; growth's smallest closure carries the three-reader contradiction once its closing sign is odd, and the even sign it makes rests on values commuting (A295); rule R (values commute exactly when some knot holds both) forces the odd sign at 12 of the 121 reached closures but changes at a birth, so it is supplied, not native.
title: No state of the whole: patterns read part by part, and values that need not commute
